component.name: grpc
component.title: gRPC
component.description: Expose gRPC services and call remote gRPC services, with Protocol Buffers messages over HTTP/2.
component.label: rpc

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

CamelGrpcMethodName.label: consumer
CamelGrpcMethodName.description: The name of the method that the client called, as the Java method name in lowerCamelCase, for example sendPing. The consumer sets it.

CamelGrpcUserAgent.label: consumer
CamelGrpcUserAgent.description: The user agent of the client that made the call, from the user-agent header of the request. The consumer sets it.

CamelGrpcEventType.label: consumer
CamelGrpcEventType.description: The event of the stream: onNext for a message, onCompleted when the stream completes, or onError when it fails. The consumer sets it for client and bidirectional streaming calls, and the producer on the exchanges that it sends to streamRepliesTo. The STREAMING producer and a producer with toRouteControlledStreamObserver read it to select the event to send.

consumerOut.description: The protobuf request message of the called method, with the method name in the CamelGrpcMethodName header. A streaming request gives one exchange per message, or with the AGGREGATION strategy a List of all its messages. forwardOnCompleted sends no body at the end of the stream, forwardOnError the Throwable

consumerReply.description: The protobuf response message of the method, or a List of them for a streaming response; no body sends an empty message. Another type is converted to the response message, or the call ends with an INTERNAL error: text, bytes, a Map or the unchanged request fail, build the message of the method. With routeControlledStreamObserver the route replies through a producer with toRouteControlledStreamObserver

producerIn.description: The protobuf request message of the method, or a List of them for a streaming request. Text, bytes or a Map fail with an argument type mismatch: build the message first

producerOut.description: A List of the protobuf response messages. With synchronous=true the response message itself, or a List of them for a streaming response. With the STREAMING strategy the body is unchanged and each response goes to the streamRepliesTo endpoint

host.description: The host name or IP address. For the consumer, the address that the gRPC server binds to, such as localhost or 0.0.0.0. For the producer, the host of the remote gRPC server.

port.description: The port. For the consumer, the port that the gRPC server listens on, where 0 lets the operating system choose a free port. For the producer, the port of the remote gRPC server.

service.description: The fully qualified name of the gRPC service: the Java package of the classes generated from the .proto file, a dot, and the service name, for example org.apache.camel.component.grpc.PingPong. The component loads the generated class of the service (PingPongGrpc in the example) by this name.

flowControlWindow.description: The HTTP/2 flow control window size in bytes of the producer. The consumer uses initialFlowControlWindow instead.

forwardOnCompleted.label: common
forwardOnCompleted.description: Whether to route an exchange without a body, with the CamelGrpcEventType header set to onCompleted, when a stream completes. The consumer does it for client and bidirectional streaming calls with the PROPAGATION or DELEGATION strategy, and the producer to the streamRepliesTo endpoint.

forwardOnError.label: common
forwardOnError.description: Whether to route an exchange with the Throwable as body, and the CamelGrpcEventType header set to onError, when a stream fails. The consumer does it for client and bidirectional streaming calls with the PROPAGATION or DELEGATION strategy, and the producer to the streamRepliesTo endpoint.

maxMessageSize.description: The maximum size in bytes of a message that the consumer or the producer receives. A larger message fails the call with the RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED status.

autoDiscoverServerInterceptors.label: consumer
autoDiscoverServerInterceptors.description: Whether the consumer intercepts the incoming calls with all the io.grpc.ServerInterceptor beans of the registry.

consumerStrategy.label: consumer
consumerStrategy.description: How the consumer handles client streaming and bidirectional streaming calls; unary and server streaming calls always give one exchange per call. AGGREGATION routes all request messages as one List when the client completes the stream, and sends the reply of the route. PROPAGATION routes each request message in its own exchange and sends its reply, unless routeControlledStreamObserver is true. DELEGATION routes each request message and sends nothing: it requires routeControlledStreamObserver.

initialFlowControlWindow.label: consumer
initialFlowControlWindow.description: The initial HTTP/2 flow control window size in bytes of the consumer. The consumer then adjusts the window to the bandwidth-delay product of the connection.

keepAliveTime.label: consumer
keepAliveTime.description: The time in milliseconds without received data after which the consumer sends a keepalive ping to the client. A value of 1000 days or more disables keepalive.

keepAliveTimeout.label: consumer
keepAliveTimeout.description: The time in milliseconds that the consumer waits for the reply to a keepalive ping before it closes the connection.

maxConcurrentCallsPerConnection.label: consumer
maxConcurrentCallsPerConnection.description: The maximum number of concurrent calls permitted for each incoming server connection. Defaults to no limit.

maxConnectionAge.label: consumer
maxConnectionAge.description: The maximum time in milliseconds that a connection exists before the consumer closes it gracefully, with a random jitter of +/-10%. A value of 1000 days or more, such as the default, means no limit.

maxConnectionAgeGrace.label: consumer
maxConnectionAgeGrace.description: The time in milliseconds that the calls in progress have to complete once maxConnectionAge is reached, before the consumer cancels them and closes the connection. A value of 1000 days or more, such as the default, means no limit.

maxConnectionIdle.label: consumer
maxConnectionIdle.description: The time in milliseconds without outstanding calls after which the consumer closes a connection gracefully. A value of 1000 days or more, such as the default, means no limit.

maxInboundMetadataSize.label: consumer
maxInboundMetadataSize.description: The maximum size in bytes of the metadata (the headers) of a call that the consumer receives.

maxRstFramesPerWindow.label: consumer
maxRstFramesPerWindow.description: The maximum number of RST_STREAM frames that the consumer accepts from a connection per maxRstPeriodSeconds, before it closes the connection. Set it together with maxRstPeriodSeconds: the consumer fails to start if only one of them is greater than 0. 0 means no limit.

maxRstPeriodSeconds.label: consumer
maxRstPeriodSeconds.description: The period in seconds of maxRstFramesPerWindow. Set it together with maxRstFramesPerWindow: the consumer fails to start if only one of them is greater than 0. 0 means no limit.

muteException.label: consumer
muteException.description: Whether the consumer leaves out the exception message from the status description that it sends to the client when the exchange fails. The description is then Exchange processing failed, and the status is INTERNAL in both cases.

permitKeepAliveTime.label: consumer
permitKeepAliveTime.description: The shortest time in milliseconds between keepalive pings that the consumer permits a client. The consumer closes the connection of a client that sends pings more often.

permitKeepAliveWithoutCalls.label: consumer
permitKeepAliveWithoutCalls.description: Whether the consumer permits clients to send keepalive pings (HTTP/2 PING frames) on a connection without outstanding calls.

routeControlledStreamObserver.label: consumer
routeControlledStreamObserver.description: Whether the route sends the responses instead of the consumer. The consumer sets the response StreamObserver of the call as the grpcResponseObserver exchange property, and the route replies with a producer with toRouteControlledStreamObserver=true. Not compatible with the AGGREGATION strategy.

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer,advanced
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exceptionHandler.label: consumer,advanced
exceptionHandler.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exchangePattern.label: consumer,advanced
exchangePattern.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

autoDiscoverClientInterceptors.label: producer
autoDiscoverClientInterceptors.description: Whether the producer intercepts the outgoing calls with all the io.grpc.ClientInterceptor beans of the registry.

inheritExchangePropertiesForReplies.label: producer
inheritExchangePropertiesForReplies.description: Whether the exchanges that the producer sends to the streamRepliesTo endpoint get a copy of the exchange properties of the exchange that made the call. For example, the replies then keep the grpcResponseObserver property for toRouteControlledStreamObserver.

method.label: producer
method.description: The name of the method that the producer calls, as in the .proto file or as the Java method name. The producer converts it to the lowerCamelCase name of the stub method, so SendPing and send_ping both call sendPing.

producerStrategy.label: producer
producerStrategy.description: How the producer calls the method. SIMPLE makes one call per exchange. STREAMING sends the body of each exchange as a message on one shared call, which needs a method with a stream request, and sends the responses to the streamRepliesTo endpoint.

streamRepliesTo.label: producer
streamRepliesTo.description: The URI of the endpoint that receives the responses of the server, one exchange per response message, with the CamelGrpcEventType header. Required with the STREAMING strategy. With the SIMPLE strategy the responses go to this endpoint instead of the body, unless synchronous is true.

toRouteControlledStreamObserver.label: producer
toRouteControlledStreamObserver.description: Whether the producer replies to the client of a consumer with routeControlledStreamObserver=true, instead of calling a server. It sends the body to the StreamObserver in the grpcResponseObserver exchange property, as the event in the CamelGrpcEventType header. The other options of the producer are not used.

userAgent.label: producer
userAgent.description: The user agent that the producer sends to the server. gRPC Java adds its own user agent after this value.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer,advanced
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

synchronous.label: advanced
synchronous.description: Whether to process synchronously. The producer then calls the method with a blocking stub and waits for the response, which methods with a stream request do not support. The consumer then routes unary and server streaming calls synchronously.

authenticationType.label: security
authenticationType.description: The authentication of the calls, in addition to the transport security. GOOGLE makes the producer send the OAuth2 access tokens of the Google service account in serviceAccountResource, and requires negotiationType TLS. GOOGLE is supported only on the producer: a consumer with GOOGLE fails to start. JWT makes the producer send a JSON Web Token signed with jwtSecret, and the consumer accept only calls with a valid token.

jwtAlgorithm.label: security
jwtAlgorithm.description: The HMAC algorithm that signs the JSON Web Token on the producer and verifies it on the consumer.

jwtIssuer.label: security
jwtIssuer.description: The issuer (iss claim) of the JSON Web Token. The producer puts it in the token, and the consumer accepts only tokens with the same issuer.

jwtMaxTokenAge.label: consumer,security
jwtMaxTokenAge.description: The maximum age of a JSON Web Token that the consumer accepts, in milliseconds, from its iat (issued at) claim. When set, the consumer rejects tokens that are older, or that have no iat claim. The consumer always rejects a token whose exp (expires at) claim has passed. The default 0 does not check the age, so tokens without an exp claim are valid until jwtSecret changes. Used when authenticationType is JWT.

jwtSecret.label: security
jwtSecret.description: The secret key of the HMAC algorithm that signs the JSON Web Token on the producer and verifies it on the consumer. Required when authenticationType is JWT.

jwtSubject.label: security
jwtSubject.description: The subject (sub claim) of the JSON Web Token. The producer puts it in the token, and the consumer accepts only tokens with the same subject.

jwtTokenLifetime.label: producer,security
jwtTokenLifetime.description: How long a JSON Web Token that the producer sends is valid, in milliseconds: the token has the iat (issued at) claim and an exp (expires at) claim this much later. The producer creates a new token when less than a tenth of the lifetime, at most one minute, is left. A value of 0 sends a token without iat and exp claims, which is valid until jwtSecret changes. Used when authenticationType is JWT.

keyCertChainResource.label: security
keyCertChainResource.description: The location of the X.509 certificate chain in PEM format. For the consumer, the certificate of the server, required with TLS. For the producer, the certificate of the client for mutual TLS, set together with keyResource.

keyPassword.label: security
keyPassword.description: The password of the private key in keyResource, if the key is encrypted.

keyResource.label: security
keyResource.description: The location of the PKCS#8 private key in PEM format of keyCertChainResource. For the consumer, the key of the server, required with TLS. For the producer, the key of the client for mutual TLS, set together with keyCertChainResource.

negotiationType.label: security
negotiationType.description: The transport security of the HTTP/2 connection: PLAINTEXT for no encryption, or TLS. With TLS the consumer requires keyCertChainResource and keyResource, and a certificate from each client.

serviceAccountResource.label: security
serviceAccountResource.description: The location of the Google Cloud service account key file in JSON format, for example classpath:service-account.json. Required when authenticationType is GOOGLE: the producer sends the OAuth2 access tokens of this account.

trustCertCollectionResource.label: security
trustCertCollectionResource.description: The location of the trusted certificates in PEM format that verify the certificate of the other side: of the server for the producer, of the clients for the consumer. For the consumer, these are the CA certificates whose client certificates the consumer accepts, required with TLS. If not set, the producer verifies the server with the default trust store of the JVM.
